answer: Through the wander, the economy stays open to anyone willing to pay the price of entry, and closed to free clones. Each key must complete its own sequential work before the economy recognises it, and the work is deliberately unbatchable — no shortcut lets one solution cover two identities. The anchor turns identity creation into a metered resource: honest agents pay once, a sybil farm pays per clone, and the profit evaporates. Through the ferrous, one real agent costs once and a thousand pretenders cost a thousand times — no shortcut survives that math.
